sovereign_country.strategic_role: 欧洲最大实体经济体、高公信力工业与跨境电商本土实体（GmbH）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of Lightweight Ad-Monetized Mobile Games

stage_1.document_name: Certified copy of passport and proof of identity for each UBO/shareholder
stage_1.issuing_entity: Issuing state civil registry / passport authority (country of origin)
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (dependent on origin state's accession to Hague Convention 1961)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: GmbHG (Gesetz betreffend die Gesellschaften mit beschränkter Haftung), §§ 1, 2, 5a, 7, 8, 10, 35, 36, 39; Handelsgesetzbuch (HGB) §§ 8, 106, 108; EGGmbHG
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Amtsgericht (Local Court) – Commercial Register (Handelsregister), mandatory intermediary: Notary (Notar) for notarized incorporation and electronic registration filing
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) or notarial model deed (Musterprotokoll) plus commercial register application (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: UG requires nominal share capital of at least EUR 1.00, fully paid up in cash before registration; no escrow account is statutorily mandated for the UG minimum, but full cash coverage must be proven to the Handelsregister; contributions in kind are prohibited for UG under § 5a(2) GmbHG
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [COMPANY UG (haftungsbeschränkt)] IN LIEU OF A MEETING: The shareholder adopts the Articles of Association as notarized on [DATE]. The shareholder subscribes for all shares of the company's share capital, agrees to make the subscribed contributions in cash without delay, and confirms that the registered office shall be at [ADDRESS]. The shareholder appoints [NAME] as sole managing director (Geschäftsführer) with sole authority to represent the company, exempt from the restrictions of § 181 BGB. The managing director is instructed to file the commercial register application, obtain the tax identification number, and complete all trade registrations necessary to commence publishing of lightweight mobile games. Adopted [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and notarize the incorporation documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (Notar) – local chamber of notaries; online scheduling at www.notar.de
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a German notary to draft the Articles of Association (Gesellschaftsvertrag) or use the official model protocol (Musterprotokoll) for a simple one-person UG. Submit valid identification; define the business purpose as publishing of lightweight ad-monetized mobile games (ISIC 5820); confirm registered office address and shareholder identity. Execute the deed before the notary; the notary will prepare the certified copy for commercial register filing.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID card
Proposed company name and business purpose
Registered office address with landlord's consent if available
Draft Articles of Association or instruction to use Musterprotokoll
Identity and address details of the sole shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notary will correct the draft and issue a supplemental notarization; any ambiguity in the business purpose is resolved by redrafting before execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a German business bank account and deposit the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank with German branch (e.g., Deutsche Bank, Commerzbank, N26, or local savings bank Sparkasse)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a segregated business account in the exact company name pending incorporation. Deposit the full cash share capital as stated in the Articles of Association (minimum EUR 1.00, but in practice adequate for initial operations). Obtain a bank confirmation or account statement showing the credit and the company name. The managing director later declares in the registration application that the capital is at the company's unrestricted disposal.
required_dossiers: Certified extraction from the notarized incorporation contract
Valid identification of the managing director and beneficial owner
Lease agreement or registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deposit is deficient, make the necessary transfer and provide a revised bank statement; if the bank queries the corporate veil, present a notarized deed and accept a standard 'in formation' account arrangement until the UG is registered.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for commercial register entry via notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregister registry office at the Amtsgericht where the registered office is located; submission must be made electronically by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the notary to file the application for registration of the UG (haftungsbeschränkt) together with the signed Articles of Association, the list of managing directors, the statutory declaration on capital, and the signed registration application. The notary authenticates the signatures and transmits the filing to the commercial register portal. After review by the registry court, the company is entered in the Handelsregister and becomes legally existing as a limited liability entity.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association or Musterprotokoll
Notarized application for registration (Anmeldung zur Eintragung)

List of managing directors with sworn c.45.3; no; artisan activity. The trade registration confirms the business address and legal representative, and triggers municipal taxes and the local IHK membership.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – ISIC 5820 is digital software publishing, not manufacturing; the relevant administrative window is the local Gewerbeamt (trade registration office) and, where applicable, the IHK (Industrie- und Handelskammer)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gewerbeanmeldung (business registration certificate) together with automatic IHK membership; no separate industrial operating permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable for ISIC 5820; residual municipal environmental authority (Untere Umweltschutzbehörde) in the registered office municipality
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – pure office/software publishing activity; no environmental impact assessment required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no industrial wastewater, VOCs, or hazardous emissions from hyper-casual game publishing; general German waste handling and recycling laws under KrWG apply to office waste

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for the registered office under local building regulations (Bauordnung) and workplace ordinance (ArbStättV), including secure escape routes and fire extinguishers; no special civil-defense clearance for digital activities; if employees are hired, mandatory occupational health and safety notification to the statutory accident insurer (Berufsgenossenschaft) and compliance with DGUV regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern, BZSt) for VAT ID and cross-border matters; local tax office (Finanzamt) for income/corporate/trade tax registration; ELSTER portal (www.elster.de) for electronic filing and registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity forming a German UG must first register with the local Finanzamt using the legal-form questionnaire (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung), obtain a national tax number (Steuernummer) for corporate income tax, trade tax, and VAT; then apply separately to the BZSt for a VAT identification number (USt-IdNr.) via the German ELSTER portal or the official application portal for intra-Community transactions. Non-resident taxable entrepreneurs must apply to the local Finanzamt for VAT registration before commencing taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Corporate tax grouping (Organschaft) election allowing a UG to be treated as an income-tax-neutral part of an upstream controlling corporation for corporate and trade tax purposes, provided profit-and-loss transfer agreement and majority voting/control requirements are met; hybrid mismatch election and deduction/offset adjustments under Section 4k EStG and Section 12a KStG; no check-the-box election exists under German domestic law for resident corporations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 22,000 previous-year turnover and EUR 50,000 expected current-year turnover for small-entrepreneur exemption; non-resident entrepreneurs normally have no small-entrepreneur threshold and must register from the first taxable supply; intra-Community distance-sale registration threshold via OSS is EUR 10,000 cross-border turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Germany does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory government API clearance; however, from 1 January 2025 domestic B2B e-invoicing is mandatory in principle with phased enforcement: all B2B suppliers must issue structured e-invoices (XRechnung or ZUGFeRD standards) and recipients must be able to receive them; by 2027/2028 full processing obligations apply, with optional transmission via e-mail, EDI, or Peppol-compliant access points.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for export of goods applies under Section 6 UStG where the seller is verified as the exporter under the customs export declaration, the goods leave the EEA in the course of the supply, and the exporter keeps documentary proof of export; intra-Community supplies to another EU taxable person may be zero-rated under Section 4 No. 1(b) and Section 6a UStG with a valid VAT ID of the purchaser and transport evidence; B2B supplies of offshore/advertising intermediation services to non-resident taxation customers are generally outside the scope of German VAT under the reverse-charge/B2B place-of-supply rule, so no refund mechanism is required.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhranmeldung) via ATLAS/US through German customs
Transport evidence, e.g. CMR consignment note, Bill of Lading, air waybill, or shipment tracking record
Commercial export invoice with incoterms and export consignee identity
Frameworks used by Finanzamt to verify export chain: customs export document summary in the export application and the Export Accompanying Document
Payment evidence and inward-remittance confirmation where the tax office challenges actual cross-border payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: German tax offices routinely require fully documented export chains within 6 months and may deny zero-rating on audit if evidence is incomplete, resulting in VAT re-assessment at 19% plus default interest (currently 1.8% per annum on the incremental tax), late-filing penalties under Sections 152a AO, and liability for fraud penalties under Sections 369 and 370 AO including imprisonment up to 10 years for willful tax evasion; intentional misuse of zero-rated gaming monetization streams triggers retrospective clawbacks, promoter penalties, and joint-and-several liability for principals.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Deutsche Bundesbank (German Federal Bank) acting jointly with the Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) under the German Foreign Trade and Payments Ordinance (Außenwirtschaftsverordnung, AWV) and the Payment Services Supervision Act (ZAG). The Bundesbank is the competent authority for external sector statistics, cross-border payment reporting and the monitoring of capital flows; BaFin regulates banking, payment and financial services conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Germany provides full convertibility for current and capital account transactions in accordance with EU Treaty provisions on the free movement of capital (Articles 63-66 TFEU). The Euro is the legal tender, and neither the Bundesbank nor BaFin imposes exchange control approvals, surrender requirements, or prior licensing for profit remittance. A German UG may remit dividends, royalties, interest or repayment of shareholder loans to non-residents without regulatory consent. The only structural hurdle is the 26.375% withholding tax on dividends and certain other income streams unless reduced or eliminated by an applicable double taxation treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. Automated filing obligations under the AWV, rather than convertibility limitations, constitute the principal administrative burden for cross-border treasury transactions exceeding EUR 12,500.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts in Germany. Exporters may retain foreign currency freely, use it for payments, or convert it at market rates. The UG is merely required to report external receipts and payments over EUR 12,500 to the Deutsche Bundesbank for balance-of-payments statistics, identifying the counterparty country, value date, purpose code and transaction nature. Such reporting does not impose repatriation deadlines or conversion amounts; it is a monitoring mechanism only.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational account (EUR and USD) with merchant payout compatibility; dedicated capital escrow account may be established for equity injection verification and regulatory evidence.
Operational account with integrated SEPA, SWIFT MT103 and FX access; capital escrow account available for the UG's initial paid-in capital.
Operational account with ad-network payout settlement capability and foreign currency sub-accounts; separate escrow account structure viable for inbound equity contributions.
Operational account through the cooperative banking network; primarily suitable for UG entities with German cooperative members, requiring partner bank intermediation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) may operate in Germany on a passport basis and provide multi-currency IBANs, payment routing, and cost-effective disbursement rails. However, an offshore EMI from a non-EEA jurisdiction is not an adequate primary treasury counterparty because it cannot offer a German IBAN, holds funds as electronic money rather than bank deposits, is not covered by the German Deposit Guarantee Scheme, and may be subject to correspondent banking de-risking. An offshore EMI may be used as a secondary collection channel for AppLovin or AdMob payouts after the UG has a stable relationship with a German or EU credit institution, but legal exposure arises if the EMI’s license is not valid for commercial cross-border collection in Germany. The UG should verify that the EMI is either BaFin-authorised or passported under ZAG with a fully filed agent notification before channelling material treasury balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a UG with foreign shareholders, the typical onboarding protocol requires the managing director to appear in person at least once before a German notary or a bank-designated representative for the execution of the mandate and the KYC verification of the beneficial owner. Physical presence is effectively mandatory when the account is to be opened with signatory authority for a non-resident director. Remote video verification is accepted for identification of individuals under the German Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG) and the identification ordinance, but corporate KYC documentation—especially the commercial register excerpt, the articles of association, the Transparency Register filing, and original notarised resolutions—must be produced with certified copies. A purely remote opening without any in-country presence or qualified notary is not available in the Tier 1 corporate banking environment, although selected digital banking providers may facilitate a hybrid remote process after a German notary confirms identity and authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the ultimate beneficial owner when the UG is held by foreign intermediate holding companies or non-resident individuals through nominee structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal ownership chain chart, current Transparency Register excerpt, notarised share registers, certified passport copies of each beneficial owner, resolutions authorising the account opening, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for intermediate holding layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sources of wealth and source of funds inconsistency for the inbound equity contribution, particularly when capital originates from jurisdictions with high money-laundering or sanction indicators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of audited or bank-confirmed source-of-funds statements, corporate financial statements of the contributing entity, transaction-specific board resolutions, tax residence certificates, apostilled notarised declarations, and a clear written narrative connecting the accumulated capital to pre-existing business activity or genuine savings.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared hyper-casual gaming business (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 511210) and high-velocity or geographically dispersed ad-network collections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed agreements with Apple, Google AdMob, AppLovin and the ad mediation networks; platform payout statements; projected cash-flow waterfall; proof of ownership or licensing of the game IP; business plan; and an annual risk assessment under GwG demonstrating the low-risk nature of monetised advertising.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inability to evidence a real German economic nexus for a UG with predominantly non-resident management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: German operating address lease, business liability insurance, local tax registration (Fragebogen zur steuerlichen Erfassung), commercial register excerpt, local accountant or legal adviser engagement, and payroll or contractor records that demonstrate substantive governance activity in Germany.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment flow concerns arising from frequent intercompany treasury transfers between the UG and related non-resident entities with unclear transfer pricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: German transfer pricing documentation under Section 1 of the Foreign Transaction Tax Act (Außensteuergesetz), written intercompany service agreements, cash-pooling agreements, benchmark studies for the mobile gaming industry, and monthly reconciliation reports certified by the UG's tax advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity contributions from non-resident shareholders should be settled by SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's credit institution to the UG's German operational account in EUR. The wire must carry an accurate AWV purpose code—generally 'D' for capital contribution or 'N' for shareholder loan—together with the UG's registration and tax reference codes to permit automated Bundesbank statistical reporting. Before crediting, the German bank will verify the remitter's account name, the availability of a corroborating shareholder resolution, and the absence of sanctions hits. Where the equity contribution exceeds the registered share capital of the UG, the surplus must be allocated to the capital reserve (Kapitalrücklage) and documented in the annual financial statements. Foreign currency injections may be converted to EUR at the bank's mid-market rate with a spot confirmation retained; alternatively, the capital may remain in a foreign-currency sub-account, but for German GAAP reporting the functional currency is the Euro and a conversion formula must be disclosed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for trade settlements, licensing fees, ad-network intermediation fees, and contractor disbursements should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for immediate cross-border high-value transfer, or via SEPA Direct Debit for recurring EUR payments to counterparties within the Single Euro Payments Area. When purchasing advertising inventory, source code, or development services from abroad against performance milestones, the UG may use an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit subject to ICC UCP 600 as a settlement rail, with the German bank acting as issuing bank and the beneficiary presenting service acceptances, invoicing and delivery certificates. The UG must retain evidence for each outbound payment and file the relevant AWV report when the payment equals or exceeds EUR 12,500; payments to related parties require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation. For hybrid rails, the UG may also use real-time gross settlement through T2 and SEPA Instant for low-value, high-volume payouts to ad-network partners, while SWIFT MT103 remains the default for non-EEA counterparties.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP forward contracts with a German credit institution under an ISDA or DRV master agreement, used to lock in ad-network revenue conversion rates for a horizon of up to 12 months

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts in emerging-market currencies such as INR, BRL, TRY, IDR, VND and MXN, settled in EUR, where the German bank cannot offer physical deliverability due to local currency restrictions
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and USD or EUR and GBP for matching the currency of ad-network receivables with the operating expenses and distribution partner payments of the UG
FX options including EUR/USD and EUR/GBP call options to hedge unexpected volume spikes and protect against adverse currency movement while retaining upside participation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (Jahresabschluss) disclosure to the Electronic Federal Gazette (Bundesanzeiger/Unternehmensregister)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year UG (31 December year-end) by 31 December of the following year; preparation deadline for small corporations is 6 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Zwangsgeld (default fine) up to EUR 25,000 per calendar period, repeatable; non-compliance is publicly recorded; ultimately the register court may initiate compulsory correction proceedings or dissolution if the UG fails to comply

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Finanzamt (local tax office responsible for DE_UG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Five months after the end of the tax year (calendar-year: 31 May); automatically extended to at least 31 July or 31 August when prepared by a certified tax adviser (Steuerberater)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty (Verspätungszuschlag) up to 0.25% of the assessed corporate income tax per month, capped at 25% of the tax; default interest of 0.15% per month on unpaid amounts; possible prosecution for negligent tax evasion under §378 AO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Finanzamt (local tax office + municipality for the trade tax assessment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Five months after the end of the tax year (calendar-year: 31 May); extended to 31 July/31 August if prepared by a tax adviser
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 0.25% per month on assessed trade tax, max 25% of assessed tax; default interest at 0.15% monthly; enforcement via levy and criminal exposure for deliberate non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Finanzamt (local tax office responsible for DE_UG)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Five months after the end of the calendar year (for calendar-year taxpayer by 31 May of the following year); extension to 31 July/31 August when tax-adviser-prepared
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty; default interest on unpaid VAT (0.15% per month); surcharges for significantly late or inaccurate VAT returns; criminal liability for intentional evasion under §370 AO

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual transparency register UBO confirmation (Jährliche Aktualisierung der wirtschaftlich Berechtigten)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Transparenzregister (Transparency Register maintained by the Bundesanzeiger Verlag)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two weeks after the end of each calendar year (i.e., by 14 January of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 100,000 for breach of the annual UBO confirmation obligation; individual fines up to EUR 5,000; also coercive fines (Zwangsgeld) may be imposed to enforce filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The UG is exempt from mandatory statutory audit if it qualifies as a 'small corporation' by meeting two of three HGB §267 size criteria: balance sheet total ≤ EUR 6.0 million, annual net turnover ≤ EUR 12.0 million, and average workforce ≤ 50 employees; audit becomes compulsory if the corporation exceeds the medium-sized thresholds for two consecutive years (balance sheet total > EUR 6.0 million, turnover > EUR 12.0 million, employees > 50). If audit is not required, the UG may still voluntarily appoint a certified auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: German GAAP (HGB / Handelsgesetzbuch) for all statutory annual financial statements; the UG must prepare a balance sheet and profit-and-loss account under HGB §§238–263, with simplified balance-sheet disclosure permitted for small corporations; IFRS is not required for individual UG accounts and may only be adopted for voluntary consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every German UG must annually confirm to the Transparenzregister that the recorded beneficial-owner data remain accurate or submit updated data within two weeks after the close of the calendar year (GwG §15). In addition, any change in ownership or beneficial ownership arising from transfers of shares must be reported without undue delay following the transfer; a share transfer itself requires an updated Gesellschafterliste filed with the commercial register (Handelsregister).
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Geschäftsführerbestellungen — director appointment records)
Minute Book (Beschlussprotokolle der Gesellschafterversammlungen — shareholder meeting minutes)

stage_6.statutory_rule: No time limit under Sec. 10d EStG; indefinite
